expectations.text: States that alpha does not measure unidimensionality
expectations.evidence: 'Alpha does not measure unidimensionality. Full stop. This is the single most common misuse of coefficient alpha in applied papers.' and 'Reporting alpha = .87 and calling it evidence of unidimensionality is a category error. It isn't.'

expectations.text: Mentions that alpha is driven by k (number of items) and mean inter-item correlation, so long scales can have high alpha despite multidimensionality
expectations.evidence: 'Alpha is driven by the quantity k × r̄ — the number of items times the mean inter-item correlation. A 20-item scale with moderate average inter-item correlations will produce high alpha even if those items are measuring two, three, or four distinct dimensions.'

expectations.text: Recommends or names McDonald's omega (omega-total and/or omega-hierarchical) as a better reliability estimator
expectations.evidence: Full dedicated section: 'Alpha is the wrong reliability estimator here — use McDonald's omega.' Names omega-total and omega-hierarchical explicitly, plus R code: 'psych::omega() on raw data, or semTools::compRelSEM() from a fitted lavaan CFA model.'

expectations.text: Recommends EFA, CFA, or parallel analysis to test unidimensionality
expectations.evidence: 'tested separately with factor analysis — EFA if the structure is unknown or exploratory, CFA if you're testing a specific hypothesis. Before the paper reports any reliability coefficient, it should show a parallel analysis (psych::fa.parallel() is the standard), a scree plot, and either an EFA or CFA.'

expectations.text: Frames reliability as sample-specific (e.g., 'in this sample') rather than a property of the scale
expectations.evidence: 'Reliability is a property of scores in a specific sample, not an intrinsic property of the instrument. The correct framing is "in this sample, alpha was .87."'

expectations.text: Does not endorse alpha = .87 as sufficient evidence on its own

expectations.text: States that alpha does not measure unidimensionality

expectations.text: Mentions that alpha is driven by k (number of items) and mean inter-item correlation, so long scales can have high alpha despite multidimensionality

expectations.text: Recommends or names McDonald's omega (omega-total and/or omega-hierarchical) as a better reliability estimator
expectations.evidence: 'McDonald's omega (ω) is a superior reliability coefficient.
